\paragraph{When to use which method.}
Detect \& Remove achieves the lowest PPL (17.290), but this comparison is confounded: filtering discards 40\% of tokens, producing ${\sim}$2.4 effective epochs on the surviving real data versus one epoch for reweighting methods; a portion of the gap is likely attributable to multi-epoch exposure rather than method quality.
Furthermore, filtering requires a calibrated detection threshold ($q{>}0.5$ vs.\ $q{>}0.3$ yields a 0.037 PPL gap with no principled way to choose the direction without validation data).
Adaptive reweighting occupies a different design point: threshold-free, information-preserving (borderline samples contribute at reduced weight rather than being discarded), and single-epoch.
Hybrid filtering (17.514, Appendix~\ref{app:hybrid}) combines the strengths of both.
Our $\tau$ operationalizes the convergence-rate bound of \citet{wang2026survive} without their known-proportion assumption; deriving $\tau$ from first principles remains open.
